title: Spiritual friendship
hookLine: Aelred of Rievaulx wrote that God is friendship

lines: AN ABBOT AND A YOUNG MONK.
YOU AND I, AND A THIRD.
cards: An English abbot named Aelred sits down to talk with a younger monk about friendship. He wrote the conversation up as a book, and it reads like a real talk between two people who trust each other.
The abbot opens it gently. Here we are, he says, you and I, and he hopes a third is with them: Christ, in the middle. A little later the young monk asks a startling question.
Scripture says God is love. Could we say God is friendship? The abbot doesn't laugh him off.

teach.b: The line the monk is reaching for is in the first letter of John: "God is love; and he that dwelleth in love dwelleth in God, and God in him." Aelred's answer, as he tells it, is honest.
Saying God is friendship is unusual, and scripture doesn't say it. But what is true of love, he will not hesitate to say of friendship. Whoever lives in friendship lives in God.
So Aelred is careful about which friendship he means.
He describes friendships built on pleasure, and friendships built on what someone can do for you. Those come and go.
Spiritual friendship is different: two people who want the good for each other, and who help each other toward God. The Bible has its own pictures of that kind of friendship.
Jonathan and David: "the soul of Jonathan was knit with the soul of David, and Jonathan loved him as his own soul."
Proverbs: "Iron sharpeneth iron; so a man sharpeneth the countenance of his friend."

And at the last supper, in a line this path heard on day six hundred thirty-five, Jesus says it himself: "Henceforth I call you not servants; for the servant knoweth not what his lord doeth: but I have called you friends."
In Christian life this shows up in plain ways. A prayer partner. Monks and nuns in community.
A small group that knows when you're struggling. Some churches name the role: a spiritual director, a sponsor, a godparent. What Aelred adds is the third person at the table.
A friendship like that has room for one more.

how: Christians often seek friends who share their faith: prayer partners, small groups, sponsors and godparents, and in some traditions a spiritual director; monastic communities treat friendship as part of the life of prayer.

o: a friendship formed online with someone far away
a bond between a person and a spirit or an angel
friends who help each other toward God, Christ in the midst

p: an abbot who wrote about friendship

s: "God is friendship" is a line straight from the Bible
Aelred admits scripture doesn't say it. he adapts the first letter of John's "God is love."
Jesus tells his disciples he calls them friends, not servants
"henceforth I call you not servants ... but I have called you friends."
in Aelred's book, every friendship counts as spiritual friendship
he sets friendships built on pleasure or advantage apart from friendship that helps each other toward God.

games.q: you're the abbot. a young monk asks: scripture says God is love, so could we say God is friendship? what do you answer?
o: no. scripture never says it, so we can't.
yes, obviously, it's the same thing.
it's unusual, but what's true of love I'll say of friendship.
games.why: Aelred admits the phrase is unusual and not in scripture, then says he won't hesitate to grant friendship what is said of love: whoever lives in friendship lives in God.

practice: Let one person come to mind who has helped you toward what's good: a friend who told you the truth when it stung, someone who just kept showing up.
Go back to one moment with them, and let a short, plain thank-you form in your head. If you pray, you can give thanks to God for them by name.

wordCard.voice: Spiritual friendship. In Aelred's picture, a friendship with Christ as the third in the room: two people who want the good for each other and help each other toward God.

orig.note: Latin: friendship, the word in the title of Aelred's book on spiritual friendship.

carryVoice: Your line: friendship is holy. Two friends, and Christ in the middle. See you tomorrow.
